definition: Updating and using probability distributions over unknowns given data.
example: Maintain uncertainty over a regression function.
caveat: Exact inference is often computationally intractable.

definition: Linear regression with a posterior distribution over coefficients.
example: Estimate uncertainty in a small regression problem.
caveat: Posterior uncertainty reflects the chosen model assumptions.

definition: A neural model that represents uncertainty over its parameters through a probability distribution or an approximation to one.
example: Estimate predictive uncertainty from weight uncertainty.
caveat: Approximate Bayesian inference can still be miscalibrated.

definition: Sequential optimization using a surrogate model and an acquisition rule to choose evaluations.
example: Tune an expensive training pipeline.
caveat: Modeling and acquisition overhead may not suit cheap evaluations.

definition: Keeping several high-scoring partial sequences while expanding candidate continuations.
example: Decode structured sequence outputs.
caveat: It can prefer bland or length-biased outputs without suitable scoring.

definition: The number of partial hypotheses retained in beam search.
example: Compare decoding with four versus eight beams.
caveat: Larger beams do not guarantee better task-level quality.

definition: Supervised learning of actions from demonstrated observations or states.
example: Train a policy to imitate recorded expert moves.
caveat: Errors can compound when the policy visits unseen states.

definition: A probability distribution over possible underlying states given available history.
example: Track uncertainty about an unseen environment state.
caveat: Exact belief updates may be intractable.

definition: A recursive relationship expressing value through immediate reward and successor value.
example: Evaluate or improve a policy.
caveat: Different Bellman equations apply to fixed and optimal policies.

definition: A standardized task, dataset, or protocol for comparing systems.
example: Evaluate multiple models under the same test procedure.
caveat: A benchmark score captures only the measured task.

definition: A distribution over a binary outcome with success probability p.
example: Model a single click versus no click.
caveat: One trial differs from a count of many trials.

definition: Naive Bayes for binary presence-or-absence features.
example: Classify documents by whether words occur.
caveat: Absence contributes information unlike simple count-only interpretations.

definition: A transformer-encoder model family pretrained using masked-token objectives to learn bidirectional text representations.
example: Adapt contextual representations for text classification.
caveat: BERT is not a standard left-to-right chat generator.

definition: A text-similarity metric aligning contextual token embeddings between candidate and reference texts.
example: Evaluate semantic overlap in generated text.
caveat: Embedding similarity does not guarantee factual faithfulness.

definition: Generating N candidates and selecting one using a scoring or verification rule.
example: Choose the highest-quality verified solution.
caveat: Selection can exploit weaknesses in the scoring rule.

definition: A 16-bit floating-point format with float32-like exponent range and fewer significand bits.
example: Train deep networks with broad numeric range and lower memory.
caveat: Range and precision are different properties.

definition: Encoding queries and candidates separately so their vectors can be compared efficiently.
example: Precompute document embeddings for search.
caveat: Separate encoding limits direct token-level query-document interaction.

definition: A structured investigation of systematic performance or outcome disparities and their causes.
example: Inspect data, labels, outputs, and subgroup metrics.
caveat: An audit is not a guarantee that all biases have been found.

definition: An additive model parameter that shifts an activation or prediction.
example: The constant term in linear regression.
caveat: Different from statistical bias or social bias.

definition: The interaction between systematic model error and sensitivity to training samples.
example: Compare a rigid linear model with a flexible tree.
caveat: The textbook decomposition relies on specified loss and assumptions.

definition: A representation using information from both earlier and later positions.
example: Encode a masked token using surrounding words.
caveat: It cannot directly serve unrestricted causal next-token prediction.

definition: A recurrent model combining forward and backward passes over a sequence.
example: Encode a fully available sentence.
caveat: It cannot use unseen future input in causal streaming.

definition: Classification with two target classes.
example: Predict whether a transaction is fraudulent.
caveat: Class imbalance can make accuracy misleading.

definition: Cross-entropy for binary targets and predicted probabilities.
example: Train independent multilabel outputs.
caveat: Stable implementations often accept logits, not probabilities.

definition: The distribution of successes across a fixed number of independent Bernoulli trials.
example: Model correct answers across independent test cases.
caveat: Independence and equal success probability are assumptions.

definition: Average coding cost per character implied by a probabilistic text model.
example: Compare character-level predictive compression.
caveat: Character definition and preprocessing affect comparisons.

definition: Combining model outputs, often using a held-out set to fit combination weights.
example: Average or weight several model predictions.
caveat: The term is used inconsistently across communities.

definition: A text-generation metric based on clipped n-gram precision with a brevity penalty.
example: Evaluate machine translation at corpus level.
caveat: It imperfectly captures meaning and is sensitive to tokenization.

definition: A lexical ranking function using term frequency, inverse document frequency, and document-length normalization.
example: Rank text documents for a keyword query.
caveat: Tokenization and domain vocabulary still affect retrieval.

definition: A multiple-testing adjustment dividing a family-wise error budget across tests.
example: Use a stricter threshold when testing many hypotheses.
caveat: It can be conservative, especially with correlated tests.

definition: Sequentially adding models to improve an ensemble's objective or correct prior weaknesses.
example: Build a strong predictor from shallow trees.
caveat: Boosting is not the same as simple model averaging.

definition: Estimating a statistic's variability by repeatedly resampling observed data with replacement.
example: Estimate an uncertainty interval for a score difference.
caveat: Respect grouped or temporal dependence when resampling.

definition: Updating an estimate using another learned estimate as part of its target.
example: Use a predicted next-state value in a TD target.
caveat: Different from statistical bootstrap resampling.

definition: A marker indicating the beginning of a sequence.
example: Initialize generation with a designated start token.
caveat: Not every model requires an explicit BOS token.

definition: A narrower representation or capacity-limited stage constraining information flow.
example: Compress data through an autoencoder's latent code.
caveat: Narrow dimension alone does not guarantee interpretable compression.

definition: A rectangular region describing an object's approximate extent.
example: Store a detector's predicted vehicle location.
caveat: Boxes include background and do not precisely describe shape.

definition: A squared-error score for probability predictions, with binary and multiclass conventions.
example: Evaluate predicted class probabilities.
caveat: It reflects more than calibration alone.

definition: Rules that align compatible tensor shapes for elementwise operations without explicitly copying every repeated value.
example: Add a bias vector to each row of a matrix.
caveat: A valid broadcast can still implement the wrong intended computation.

definition: Representing unsupported text units using their underlying bytes.
example: Avoid unknown tokens for unusual characters.
caveat: Fallback can increase token count substantially.

definition: Tokenization based on byte representations, optionally merged into larger units.
example: Represent arbitrary text without a conventional unknown word.
caveat: Bytes are not the same as Unicode characters.

definition: A tokenization method building larger units by repeatedly merging frequent adjacent pairs.
example: Construct a subword vocabulary.
caveat: Byte-level BPE and character-initialized BPE use different initial units.

definition: Agreement between predicted probabilities and observed frequencies under a defined evaluation.
example: Among predictions near 0.8, check whether about 80% are correct.
caveat: Calibration differs from ranking ability and quantization calibration.

definition: Representative examples used to estimate quantization statistics or other calibration parameters.
example: Measure activation ranges before quantization.
caveat: Quantization calibration differs from probability calibration.

definition: Releasing a new version to a limited share of real traffic before broader rollout.
example: Check model behavior on a small production slice.
caveat: A small traffic slice can miss rare failures.

definition: Testing what a system can accomplish under specified conditions and assistance.
example: Measure coding success with a fixed tool budget.
caveat: Poor results can reflect elicitation or scaffolding limitations.

definition: Failure because a system cannot successfully perform a task, rather than because it pursues a different objective.
example: A model lacks the reasoning ability to solve a problem.
caveat: Observed failure alone may not reveal the cause.

definition: Loss of previously learned behavior when training on new data or tasks.
example: A fine-tuned model loses earlier capabilities.
caveat: Forgetting and beneficial specialization can be hard to separate.

definition: A gradient-boosted-tree library with specialized techniques for categorical features and prediction shift.
example: Model mixed numeric and categorical tabular data.
caveat: Categorical handling still requires proper train-test separation.

definition: Cross-entropy over a categorical target distribution.
example: Train a single-label multiclass classifier.
caveat: Do not apply softmax twice when the loss accepts logits.

definition: A probability distribution over a finite set of categories.
example: Sample a token from a vocabulary distribution.
caveat: Describes one categorical draw, not a count vector.
